title: The Sunset Club: Pete Brown, Pete Johnson, Joe Turner and the Rex Stewart session
summary: Lips Page takes Leeman to the black Sunset Club, where he is the only white musician admitted; he hears Pete Brown, Pete Johnson and Joe Turner and sees Lips challenge Rex Stewart.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yes, and I'd spend every minute of my time there, and Lips would take me to a club called the Sunset, which is a black club, now. They had race laws then. They didn't allow any white in the Sunset Club where Joe Turner was working and Pete Brown.
Pete Brown, what did he play?
Saxophone.
Right.
Alto saxophone.
What kind of saxophone player was he? How'd you like him?
Oh, nothing like I never heard before.
Same here, I agree with you.
This is how I was digesting -- I was listening.
Okay, I wish you'd tell about these guys.
Well, Duke Ellington came into town, and ...
Well, what about Pete Brown?

I would go up after work, which would be six o'clock in the morning, on Monday mornings, which would be ten o'clock in the morning, we'd all got to Sunset, which went to twelve o'clock, and Pete Brown, and the piano player was the other. Pete ... oh, what was his name.
Pete Johnson?

Yes, Pete Johnson. And then everybody would get off from work. Basie had a set with the police department up there -- there were some very big cats with clubs, and no white was allowed, but I was allowed.
Well, tell about that.
I guess I was passing.
Yeah, you were passing because you were a musician, and most musicians ...

When I would get there, they would have sessions for an hour-and-a-half or two hours -- I was there when Rex [Stewart] came from Duke Ellington's band, and in those days everybody would say he won't do it -- but he did. Lips Page challenged him.
Challenged who?
Rex.
Were you the only white musician there?
That's right, ever -- in that club.
Uh huh.
And I've seen people go crazy, the music was so great, what with Joe Turner singing the blues and ...
